items.group: Tools Drydock runs or you install
items.name: osv-scanner
items.role: The dependency vulnerability check (sends package names to osv.dev unless run offline). Comes with Drydock's Windows download (decision P77: pinned in packaging/bundle.json, fetched by cmd/drydock-bundle in CI and checked against GitHub's SHA-256 digest, installed from the download's tools folder at the first start). The Security page offers newer releases (a check three minutes after start and twice a day, or Check for updates) and Update installs one from google/osv-scanner's GitHub releases, checked the same way (decision P66).
items.note: 2.7.0 was built from the Go module proxy and run for real on 2026-10-16 in the development sandbox: the deps check's and the security scan's exact invocations (scan source --format json -r .) with the offline databases (api.osv.dev is not reachable from there); it read go.mod and ui/package-lock.json, found the module-level advisory GO-2026-5932 on golang.org/x/crypto's openpgp (not imported by Drydock; govulncheck agrees) and GHSA-wq5f-xc86-pv6w on sharp 0.35.4 in the Cloudflare starter fixture, and its JSON is read by checks.ParseOSV (the captured output is internal/checks/testdata/osv-scanner-2.7.0.json).

items.group: Tools Drydock runs or you install
items.name: Opengrep (the security scan's Code engine)
items.role: The Code engine of the security scan (decision P44): a Semgrep-compatible static analyser, LGPL-2.1, native Windows binary. Comes with Drydock's Windows download, pinned in packaging/bundle.json and checked against GitHub's SHA-256 digest (decision P77); the Security page offers newer releases and Update installs one from opengrep/opengrep's GitHub releases (decision P66). It runs with Drydock's built-in rules (internal/scan/rules) and, if the person adds one, a folder of their own.
items.note: Built-in rules (decision P77): Drydock's own 34 rules and two MIT sets copied at a fixed commit, dgryski/semgrep-go (66 rules, Go) and 0xdea/semgrep-rules (49 rules, C and C++); internal/scan/rules/README.md names the commits. Not built in, on licence grounds: opengrep-rules (LGPL-2.1 with the Commons Clause, 'for research, testing & benchmarking'), semgrep-rules (Semgrep Rules License) and trailofbits/semgrep-rules (AGPL-3.0). Newest release read from GitHub's tags.

items.group: Tools Drydock runs or you install
items.name: Docker-compatible container engine (docker)
items.role: The container engine of the per-task sandbox (decision P30, docs/sandbox.md): Docker Desktop or another Docker-compatible engine you install; Drydock runs only the docker command and never bundles an engine. The egress proxy image it starts is built from this repository (cmd/drydock-egress) and imported locally, not pulled.
items.note: Version shown is the Docker Engine and CLI the sandbox is tested with on Linux: 29.9.2 on the development host since 2026-10-21 (decision P81, from Docker's apt repository), where its daemon ran the sandbox tests as CI's sandbox job runs them (DRYDOCK_REQUIRE_DOCKER=1: 24 passed, none skipped); CI's ubuntu-latest image carries its own engine. Drydock uses only long-standing docker commands (network create --internal, import, run, exec, inspect), so any current release should work; Docker Desktop on Windows is unverified.

items.role: The CI runners (decision P56) run GitHub's own runner for a person's private repositories: unpacked on the PC for Windows jobs, built into a container image (FROM ubuntu:24.04, the current Ubuntu LTS) for Linux jobs.
items.note: Not pinned: Drydock downloads the newest stable release when a runner starts and runs it only after checking its SHA-256 against the one the release notes publish (GitHub stops serving runners that fall far behind). items.name: Git (Drydock runs it for every repository; Git for Windows on a PC)
items.role: Version control for every project: Drydock runs git for worktrees, commits, merges and the repository guard (internal/git), always with hooks, filters and external programs switched off. On a PC it is Git for Windows, which the person installs; nothing is bundled.
items.note: The version shown is the git the development host tests with (git --version): 2.56.0, built from the v2.56.0 tag of github.com/git/git into /usr/local on 2026-10-21 (decision P81) because Ubuntu 24.04 ships 2.43.0 and the host's network reaches neither kernel.org nor the git-core PPA; the full Go suite passes on it. CI's Windows jobs use the Git for Windows of GitHub's windows-latest image, which is not pinned. Drydock uses only long-standing git commands; a person's PC keeps its own Git for Windows, which its installer updates.

items.role: Development only: Semgrep OSS runs the built-in Opengrep rules against their fixtures (internal/scan builtin_rules_test.go with DRYDOCK_RULES_ENGINE) and made the SARIF fixture of the reader. Opengrep reads the same rule syntax; Semgrep is not shipped.

items.group: Tools Drydock runs or you install
items.name: llama.cpp (the local models' engine, decision P65)
items.role: The local models' engine (decision P65, docs/local-models.md): Drydock downloads the newest weekly Windows build of ggml-org/llama.cpp for the chosen backend and runs its llama-server on the person's PC as a provider. MIT.
items.note: Not pinned: when a person presses Install or Update, Drydock installs the newest release that carries the backend's archive with a SHA-256 digest (the weekly builds are tagged bNNNN and marked pre-release; the vX.Y.Z tags carry no binaries). The version shown is the newest build at the last audit. The download itself carries the TurboQuant fork's build (tool:llama.cpp-turboquant). A CUDA build is installed with the matching NVIDIA CUDA runtime archive (cudart-llama-bin-win-cuda-<toolkit>-x64.zip) from the same release, checked the same way; it follows the build.

items.group: Tools Drydock runs or you install
items.name: llama.cpp TurboQuant fork (comes with the download, Vulkan build, decision P77)
items.role: The llama.cpp build that comes installed with Drydock's Windows download (decision P77, the owner's words: 'I want it already installed with Google's TurboQuant built in'): AtomicBot-ai/atomic-llama-cpp-turboquant, MIT, a community fork of llama.cpp adding Google's TurboQuant KV cache types (turbo4, turbo3). Pinned in packaging/bundle.json for the Vulkan backend (any recent GPU), checked against GitHub's SHA-256 digest, installed at the first start with turbo4 as the cache type. Newer builds are offered on the Providers page with the twice-daily check.
items.note: The fork has not been reviewed by Drydock's maintainers; the Providers page says so. Its releases are tagged bNNNN-X.Y.Z (the llama.cpp build it is based on, then its own version); b10298-2.0.0 (2026-10-05) is the newest. Its per-commit tags (turboquant-windows-x64-vulkan-<commit>) and dev-latest are pre-release dev builds, which Drydock does not install. It trails upstream llama.cpp. Newest release tag, read from the git tags: GitHub's release listing could not be read here, so whether it is a pre-release or carries the Windows build was not checked.
